title: All Eyes on the Ranker: Participatory Auditing to Surface Blind Spots in Ranked Search Results

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative analysis of user feedback during participatory auditing workshops, where end-users interacted with a custom search interface (comparing BM25 and MonoT5 rankers) using the query 'famous doctor' and annotated perceived demographic homogeneity (e.g., the overrepresentation of men) in the top results.

Participatory auditing workshops where users qualitatively evaluated search rankings for regional and cultural omissions, identifying an overrepresentation of Western/European figures and English-centric perspectives in the retrieved biographies.

Collaborative cause-and-effect mapping activities where participants discussed and documented the downstream impacts of algorithmic curation, explicitly identifying political polarization, agenda-setting effects, and partisan skew as systemic search biases.
